At 1248 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 4.5 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

flash flooding.

areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Harlan, Loyall, Evarts, Kildav, Bailey Creek, Verda, Darkmont,
Putney, Ages, Short Town, Kenvir, Coxton, Colts, Black Mountain,
Nolansburg, Shields, Rosspoint, Golden Ash, Chevrolet and Lenarve.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 1130 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a slow-moving thunderstorm
over Kinross, or 15 miles northeast of Sigourney, moving east at 15
mph.

HAZARD...Minor flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Slowing or redirecting of traffic due to ponding or flowing
water. Closure of waterfront access due to flooding.

Locations impacted include...
Wellman, Kinross, and Amish.

Rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch have fallen from around Kinross to
north of Wellman and an additional 0.5 to 1 inch is possible.
This rain falling on saturated ground will likely result in ponding
water in low lying and poorly drained areas. This rain is also
falling on portions of the English and Skunk River basins and could
result in some renewed rises.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Southwest San Juan Mountains; San Juan River Basin
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, San Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The ground remains saturated from recent heavy rainfall over the
past week. After a brief break, deep moisture is expected to
return to southwest Colorado Tuesday with a few inches of
rainfall possible during the Wednesday through Thursday
timeframe. In addition, multiple rounds of showers and
thunderstorms are expected Wednesday through Thursday evening
producing periods of heavy rainfall and potential flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
